reformulation: Exact affine-component bijection of the analysis agent's own committed MPS (run dir test75-nomf-B1): 48,950/98,021/292,875 -> 38,001/72,968/242,048 vars/rows/nonzeros. 10,949 columns and 25,053 rows removed, 24,444 retained rows rewritten by exact substitution and 72,968 retained rows unchanged in name and sense. 9,578 two-term affine relations (4,668 unit-coefficient equalities plus 4,910 opposite-inequality pairs) span 2,146 components over 11,720 variables; 12 components are forced constant by member bounds (24 columns), 1,328 original FX columns and 35 degree-one integer leaf sums complete the removal. Objective identically zero; no new columns, cuts or aliases.
claim_class: 4 claims (integer, LP) x (forward, reverse) as exact bijections on the retained coordinates: claim = {reverse,input_integers,output_integers,objective:Equal,projection:38,001 pairs,inverse}, inverse pairing 0<->1 and 2<->3. Kernel obligations 273,923 / 320,874 / 235,922 / 271,924 = 1,102,643 discharged by 50,253 / 16,641 / 50,253 / 10,568 steps, with branches 0 and peak_live_facts 50,253 in the verify statistics.
representation_gap: Proof bytes are set by how each obligation is encoded, not by the size of the edit, and the two same-family edits show it. This certificate: 37,269,768 B (35.5 MiB, RPA 2 tier) for 1,102,643 obligations = 33.8 B per obligation, every obligation a flat Lin/EqPair fact over at most 9 terms (median step 101 B, max 250 B, branches 0). The test74 edit of the same 48,950-var/98,021-row model: 196,090,550 B (187.0 MiB = 73 percent of the 256 MiB text cap, RPA 7 tier) for 473,762 obligations = 413.9 B per obligation, because it discharges via 257,120 nested-Cases branch nodes that restate the whole goal at every node (max single step 6,064 B) plus one IntervalLift whose intervals+body payload alone is 150,757,365 B, 77 percent of that RPA (max body step 121,556 B). The 12.2x per-obligation cost is a representation choice; only a price computed before assembly can drive it, because the cheap form sits 5.3x under the cap and the expensive one at 73 percent of it.
claims: cases/test75/request.json (2,041,152 B) is a bare 4-element claim array, not the V3 request object: tools/prepare_test75.py:111 writes it as cert['claims'] again, and :104 sets inverse=[1,0,3,2][i] so the integer and LP claims of one direction pair with each other.

Each projection list is 510,178 B = 38,001 [source,target] pairs; lists 0 and 2 are identical, 1 and 3 are identical, and 1 is the exact reverse of 0 (parsed from cases/test75/request.json), so 2,040,712 of 2,041,152 B (99.98 percent) is one coordinate table restated four times.

Obligation counts 273,923 / 320,874 / 235,922 / 271,924 (cases/test75/preparation.json:31) equal the verify counter obligations:1102643 with branches:0, peak_live_facts:50253, linear_terms:421824 (cases/test75/preparation.json:91).

Block 0 checks are typed atoms, not derivations: 38,001 VarLower + 38,001 VarUpper + 38,001 VarInt + 5,982 RowEq + 42,542 RowUpper + 35,393 Local refs + 76,003 literal 'Exact' (measured in cases/test75/proof.rpa), i.e. the same row-by-row obligation plan that test74 had to express as case trees.

Four mutations are rejected with exit 2 (cases/test75/preparation.json:114): wrong_opposite_row reuses the positive inequality leg, wrong_affine_recovery changes a reconstruction constant, missing_leaf_term drops a leaf term, missing_inverse drops one coordinate from the composition.
proof_encoding: 'RPA 2' header plus compact JSON (tools/prepare_test75.py:111). Version 2 is the lowest sufficient tier: crates/core/src/rpa.rs:42 rejects a certificate whose required version exceeds the header, and crates/core/src/codec.rs:500-503 raises the requirement to 2 only for EqPair/Cases, while IntervalLift (codec.rs:488) and complete-domain bijections (codec.rs:473) force 5 and 7.

Steps: 127,715 = 115,215 Lin + 12,500 EqPair; the EqPair census decomposes exactly as 9,820 RowUpper/RowUpper legs (4,910 opposite-inequality pairs x 2 blocks), 2,656 VarLower/VarUpper (1,328 FX columns x 2) and 24 Local/VarUpper (12 bounds-forced components x 2) = 6,250 per forward block, matching tools/prepare_test75.py:26-33 and :56-62.

Byte split of the 37,269,768 B RPA: Return.checks 16,455,709 (44.2 percent, mean 14.9 B per check), steps 11,949,876 (32.1 percent), Return.map 6,695,096 (18.0 percent), inline claims 2,041,146 (5.5 percent); max step 250 B.

Duplication is structural: blocks[0].steps == blocks[2].steps byte-for-byte (50,253 steps, 4,811,573 B = 12.9 percent of the RPA) and map[0]==map[2], map[1]==map[3] (6,695,096 B, 18.0 percent); docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:380-381 records that shared expression/mapping DAGs and dedicated batch records are not implemented by this wire layout, so each domain carries its own copy.

Depth 1 with no payload end at all: interval_lifts 0, flow_lifts 0, menu_lifts 0, branches 0 (cases/test75/preparation.json:91), whereas test74's two blocks are depth 9 with branches 257,120 and interval_lifts 1 (cases/test74/preparation.json:300,312,321).
agent_manual_work: 18 eval cells / 50,014 characters of Python (digest Transcript section) hand-rolled an exact MPS reader (Fraction, INTORG marker, UP/LO/FX records), a row-shape census and a per-row interval box test - all of which the kernel already owns behind canonical and inspect-model.

The edit itself was the agent's work: an exhaustive scan of two-term unit-coefficient rows (4,668 equalities, 4,910 opposite inequality pairs), graph traversal into 2,146 components with bound intersection, and the 35 degree-one leaf sums, reported in output/report.md section 3.

It wrote a second independent checker output/verify.py (13,886 B; parse_mps:14, interval:96, main:104) plus a 10,380,373 B audit.json whose keys removed_variables / removed_rows / changed_retained_rows / affine_relations / affine_components / leaf_definitions are the only machine-readable statement of the edit.

Relation kinds were re-sorted by hand into different proof obligations (single-row equality vs two-row antisymmetry vs FX bound pair vs leaf sum), and the 24,444 rewritten retained rows carry no kernel-recorded provenance of the substitution that produced them.
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test75.py is 132 lines and imports 13 names from five sibling preparers: parse_mps,row_ref (prepare_affine:6), expression,plus,mul,expr_json,row_fact,sha (prepare_test40:7), substitute (prepare_test57:8), Builder (prepare_test88:9), fact,box,exact (prepare_test54:10).

The only rule constructors are dict emitters: Builder (prepare_test88.py:18) with refexpr (:24) and eqpair (:44); fact() (prepare_test54.py:20) chooses between a shared ref, the literal 'Exact' and a new Lin; box() (prepare_test54.py:26) emits the interval check; exact() (:16) tests whether a row is an identity.

The affine algebra is caller code: scale=1/p.refexpr(r)[1][x] (:29) recovers the pivot, cs,ct=s*ps,s*pt+t (:44) propagates the signed decomposition, :56-59 combines two one-sided bound facts into p.eqpair, :67-70 rebuilds the leaf sum from the defining row minus already-proved aliases.

One 30-line loop (:73-103) plans all four claims: variable bound and Int checks, then per output row a choice between a direct ref, 'Exact', box() and eqpair(box(e),box(-e)), then objective 'Exact', the 38,001 projection 'Exact' checks and the inverse-composition Eq facts.
main() (:110-131) owns canonical/assemble/verify orchestration plus four copy.deepcopy mutations, and records rpa_bytes only after the file already exists (cases/test75/preparation.json:46).
friction: Blocks are self-contained, so the fact prefix is copied rather than referenced: Builder(a,[counter],facts) with builder.steps=list(prefix) (:76-78) re-emits all 50,253 steps for the LP claim, 4,811,573 B = 12.9 percent of the RPA.

The 38,001-pair projection is restated per claim with no way to reuse claim 0's list (2,040,712 B = 99.98 percent of request.json) and the claim pairing is a hand-computed index table [1,0,3,2][i] (:104).

The edit arrives as an untyped 10,380,373 B audit document; the preparer re-validates four facts by hand (:15-18) and then trusts 10,949 reconstruction records, 9,578 relations and 2,146 component records while re-deriving each fact from canonical rows.
Premise wiring is implicit: the negative leg of each EqPair is the paired opposite row and the scale factor is recovered from the parsed row (:29) because the audit carries neither.

16.4 s of preparation (cases/test75/preparation.json:44) goes to parsing 17,578,309 B of MPS twice and Fraction arithmetic, although the same run had already canonicalized both models to .mcm (:117-118).
notes: Cross-case caution: cases/test74 and cases/test75 share the model family (both 48,950 vars / 98,021 rows / 292,875 nonzeros, both canonicalize to a 12,870,525 B mcm) but their run inputs are differently labelled/ordered copies - 13,301,857 of 17,578,329 bytes differ and the canonical mcm hashes differ (0eba6ee4... vs 41c34ecc...) - so the 5.3x gap is a representation comparison, not a byte-identical-input comparison. All sizes are raw bytes from the named files.
